nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathscr{F}^*$ is $\sigma$-compact. There exists $\mathscr{F}^* = \bigcup_{N=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{G}_N$ where each family $\mathscr{G}_N$ is compact. By taking finite unions, we may assume without loss of generality that $\mathscr{G}_1 \subseteq \mathscr{G}_2 \subseteq \cdots$. Let $A \in \mathscr{F}$. Since $\mathscr{G}_1 \subseteq \mathscr{F}^*$, the set $A$ belongs to $\mathscr{G}_1^*$. Since $\mathscr{G}_1$ is compact, there exists a finite set $A_1' \subseteq A$ such that $A_1' \in \mathscr{G}_1^*$. Since all members of $\mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{F}^*$ are infinite, for all $B \in \mathscr{F}^*$, the set $A \cap B$ is infinite, whereby \[ \big(A \backslash A_1' \big) \cap B \neq \emptyset. \] Since $B \in \mathscr{F}^*$ was arbitrary, we see that $A \backslash A_1' \in \mathscr{F}$. Repeating the argument for $A \backslash A_1'$ in place of $A$, we get a finite set $A_2' \subseteq A \backslash A_1'$ such that $A_2' \in \mathscr{G}_2^*$. By the same argument as before, the set $A \backslash (A_1' \cup A_2')$ is a member of $\mathscr{F}$, allowing us to continue on as before. Repeating ad infinitum, we get a sequence $A_1'$, $A_2'$, \dots of disjoint, finite subsets of $A$ such that for all $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the set $A_N' \in \mathscr{G}_N^*$. Define $A_1 \vcentcolon= A_1' \cup A_3' \cup \cdots$ and $A_2 \vcentcolon= A_2' \cup A_4' \cup \cdots$. By appending any elements in $A \backslash (A_1 \cup A_2)$ to $A_1$, we may assume that $A = A_1 \cup A_2$. We need only to show that $A_1$ and $A_2$ are members of $\mathscr{F}$. Indeed, since $\mathscr{F}^* = \bigcup_{N=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{G}_N$, we see that $\mathscr{F} = (\mathscr{F}^*)^* = \bigcap_{N=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{G}_N^*$. Since $\mathscr{G}_1^* \supseteq \mathscr{G}_2^* \supseteq \cdots$, by the construction of the $A_i$'s, both $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to $\bigcap_{N=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{G}_N^*$.

nodes.name: Families whose members split in two
nodes.statement: In view of \cref{prop:sigma-compact-implies-partition-to-two} and the examples of $\sigma$-compact families presented in \cref{sec:compact-sigma-compact-first}, every set in the following list of families can be partitioned into two sets in the same family: \begin{enumerate} \item sets of topological recurrence (dual of sets of the form in \eqref{eq:sigma_compact_topological}), \item sets of measurable recurrence (dual of sets of the form in \eqref{eq:sigma_compact_measurable}), \item sets of Bohr recurrence (dual of Bohr$_0$ sets), \item sets of pointwise recurrence for $k$-step nilsystems (dual of Nil$_k$-Bohr$_0$ sets). \end{enumerate} These facts are well known to experts, but the framing in terms of compactness is, as far as we know, new.

nodes.statement: Suppose the properties in \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_one} and \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two} hold. We will show that the property in \eqref{eqn_key_property_to_refute_sigma_compactness_one} holds for the same sets $B_1$, $B_2$, \dots. Let $B \in \mathscr{G}$ be such that $B \subseteq \bigcup_ {i=1}^\infty B_i$. By \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_one}, there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $|B \cap (B-n)| = \infty$. Writing $B = B \cap \bigcup_{i=1}^\infty B_i$, we see that \[B \cap (B-n) = \bigcup_{i,j = 1}^\infty \big( B \cap B_i \cap (B-n) \cap (B_j - n)\big).\] By \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two}, there exists $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if $\max(i,j) > d$, then $B_i \cap (B_j - n) = \emptyset$. Therefore, \[B \cap (B-n) = \bigcup_{i,j = 1}^d \big( B \cap B_i \cap (B-n) \cap (B_j - n)\big) \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^d \big( B \cap B_i \big).\] By assumption, the set on the left hand side is infinite, so there must exist an $i \in \{1, \ldots, d\}$ such that $B \cap B_i$ is infinite. This verifies \eqref{eqn_key_property_to_refute_sigma_compactness_one}.

nodes.statement: Suppose $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is piecewise syndetic. There exists a syndetic set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a thick set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $B = S \cap H$. There exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\bigcup_{i=1}^N (S-i) = \mathbb{N}$, and so $\bigcup_{i=1}^N (B-i) \supseteq \bigcap_{i=1}^N (H-i)$. It follows that the set \[ B \cap \bigcup_{i=1}^N (B-i) \supseteq S \cap H \cap \bigcap_{i=1}^N (H-i) \] is piecewise syndetic. Since the family $\mathcal{PS}$ is partition regular, there exists $n \in \{1, \ldots, N\}$ such that the set $B \cap (B-n)$ is piecewise syndetic.

We will show that $d\mathcal{T}$ and $dc\mathcal{T}$ satisfy the conditions in \cref{lemma_suff_condition_for_key_property_for_dual_not_sigma_compact} and hence in \eqref{eqn_key_property_to_refute_sigma_compactness_one}. To see that \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_one} holds for $d\mathcal{T}$ and $dc\mathcal{T}$, let $B \in d\mathcal{T}$ or $B \in dc\mathcal{T}$. By \cref{thm_dy_c_thick_is_ps}, the set $B$ is piecewise syndetic. Thus, by \cref{lem:piecewise_syndetic_shift}, there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ for which the set $B \cap (B-n)$ is piecewise syndetic and hence infinite. We will show that property \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two} in \cref{lemma_suff_condition_for_key_property_for_dual_not_sigma_compact} holds for the family $d\mathcal{T}$. Since $d\mathcal{T} \subseteq dc\mathcal{T}$, it will follow that $dc\mathcal{T}$ also satisfies \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two}. Let $\{T_{i,j} \ | \ i, j \in \mathbb{N}\}$ be a doubly-indexed family of thick subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that are well separated, in the sense that  egin{align} \lim_{d 	o \infty} \min  igcup_{\substack{ i, j, k, \ell \in \mathbb{N} \ (i,j) 
eq (k, \ell) \ \max(i,j,k,\ell) > d}} \min  ig(T_{i,j} - T_{k,\ell}  ig) = \infty, \end{align} where the notation $(i,j)$ denotes an element of $\mathbb{N}^2$. Let $p_1, p_2, \ldots$ be an increasing enumeration of the primes. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, define \[B_i =  igcup_{j = i}^\infty  ig(T_{i,j} \cap (p_j \mathbb{N} + 1)  ig).\] The sets $B_1$, $B_2$, \dots are disjoint, and by \cref{rem:combinatorial_primes}, each is dynamically thick. To verify the limit in \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two}, note that for all $i, k \in \mathbb{N}$, \[B_i - B_k =  igcup_{\substack{j=i\ \ell = k}}^\infty \Big (  ig( T_{i,j} \cap (p_j \mathbb{N} + 1)  ig) -  ig( T_{k,\ell} \cap (p_\ell \mathbb{N} + 1)  ig) \Big) \subseteq  igcup_{\substack{j=i\ \ell = k}}^\infty  ig( T_{i,j} - T_{k,\ell}  ig).\] For all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, considering the cases $i=k$ and $i 
eq k$ separately, we see that \[\min  igcup_{\substack{i,k = 1 \ \max(i,k) > d}}^\infty  ig( B_i - B_k ig) \geqslant \min  igg(  igcup_{\substack{ i, j, k, \ell \in \mathbb{N} \ (i,j) 
eq (k, \ell) \ \max(i,j,k,\ell) > d}} \min  ig(T_{i,j} - T_{k,\ell}  ig), p_{d}  igg).\] The limit in \eqref{eqn_suff_condition_for_key_prop_two} follows now from the limit in \eqref{eqn_very_well_separated_thick_sets} and the fact that $\lim_{d 	o \infty} p_d = \infty$, as desired.

nodes.statement: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. \begin{enumerate} \item The set $A$ is \emph{dynamically piecewise syndetic} if there exists a dynamically syndetic set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a dynamically thick set $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A = B \cap C$. The family of dynamically piecewise syndetic sets is \[d\mathcal{PS} \vcentcolon= d\mathcal{S} \sqcap d\mathcal{T}.\] \item The set $A$ is \emph{dynamically central piecewise syndetic} if there exists a dynamically central syndetic set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a set of pointwise recurrence $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A = B \cap C$. The family of dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets is \[dc\mathcal{PS} \vcentcolon= dc\mathcal{S} \sqcap dc\mathcal{T}.\] \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Return times of distal points are dcPS* sets
nodes.statement: Let $(X, T) $ be a system, $x \in X$ be a distal point, and $U \subseteq X$ be an open neighborhood of $x$. We claim that the set $R_T(x,U)$ is a $dc\mathcal{PS}^*$ set. Indeed, by \cref{lemma_class_cap_is_pr}, it suffices to show that for all $B \in dc\mathcal{S}$, the set $R_T(x,U) \cap B \in dc\mathcal{S}$. Let $B \in dc\mathcal{S}$. There exists a minimal system $(Y,S)$, a point $y \in Y$, and an open set $V \subseteq Y$ containing $y$ such that $R_S(y,V) \subseteq B$. By \cite[Thm. 9.11]{furstenberg_book_1981}, the point $(x,y) \in X \times Y$ is $T \times S$ uniformly recurrent, whereby the set $R_{T \times S}((x,y), U \times V) = R_T(x,U) \cap R_S(y,V)$ is dynamically central syndetic. It follows that $R_T(x,U) \cap B \in dc\mathcal{S}$, as desired.

nodes.statement: Because the families $d\mathcal{S}$ and $d\mathcal{T}$ are translation invariant (by \cref{lemma_translates_of_dsyndetic_sets,lemma_translates_of_dthick_sets}), it follows by \cref{lemma_idempotent_classcap_is_idempotent} that the family $d\mathcal{PS} = d\mathcal{S} \sqcap d\mathcal{T}$ is translation invariant, showing \eqref{item_all_translates_are_dps}. To see \eqref{item_some_translates_are_dcps}, because $A$ is dynamically piecewise syndetic, there exists a dynamically syndetic set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a dynamically thick set $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A = B \cap C$. By \cref{lemma_translates_of_dsyndetic_sets}, there are dynamically syndetically many $n$'s for which $B-n$ is dynamically central syndetic. By \cref{lemma_translates_of_dthick_sets}, for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the set $C-n$ is dynamically thick. Therefore, the set in \eqref{eqn_translates_of_dps_set} is dynamically syndetic, as desired. nodes.statement: Since $\mathscr{F}$ and $\mathscr{G}$ are filters, the family $\mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{G}$ is a filter. Thus, to see that it is a syndetic filter, it suffices to show that for all $A \in \mathscr{F}$ and $B \in \mathscr{G}$, the set $A \cap B$ is syndetic. Let $A \in \mathscr{F}$, $B \in \mathscr{G}$, and $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be thick. Since the set $A$ is central syndetic, by \cref{cor_central_syndetic_is_strongly_central}, the set $A \cap H$ is central. Since $B \in \mathcal{C}^*$, the set $A \cap H \cap B$ is nonempty. Because $H$ was an arbitrary thick set, we see that the set $A \cap B$ is syndetic, as desired. Finally, that $\mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{G}$ is idempotent follows immediately from \cref{lemma_idempotent_classcap_is_idempotent} and the idempotency of $\mathscr{F}$ and $\mathscr{G}$.

nodes.statement: \eqref{item_central_star_class_cap} \ Suppose that $\mathscr{G}$ is a $\mathcal{C}^*$, idempotent filter. To see that $\mathscr{G} \subseteq dc\mathcal{PS}^*$, it suffices by \cref{lemma_class_cap_is_pr} to show that for all $A \in dc\mathcal{S}$ and $B \in \mathscr{G}$, the set $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{S}$. Let $A \in dc\mathcal{S}$ and $B \in \mathscr{G}$. By \cref{thm_dcs_iff_cs}, the set $A$ belongs to a syndetic, idempotent filter $\mathscr{F}$. By \cref{prop:general_abstract_intersection_filter_nonsense}, the family $\mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{G}$ is a syndetic, idempotent filter. Since $A \cap B \in \mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{G}$, we have by \cref{thm_dcs_iff_cs} that $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{S}$, as desired. \eqref{item_syndetic_trans_inv_star_class_cap} \ Suppose that $\mathscr{G}$ is a syndetic, translation-invariant filter. By \cref{lemma_condition_on_subfamily_of_ps_star}, the family $\mathcal{PS}^*$ contains all syndetic, translation-invariant filters, so we have that $\mathscr{G} \subseteq \mathcal{PS}^* \subseteq \mathcal{C}^*$. Note that $\mathscr{G}$ is idempotent because it is translation invariant. To see that $\mathscr{G} \subseteq d\mathcal{PS}^*$, it suffices by \cref{lemma_class_cap_is_pr} to show that for all $A \in d\mathcal{S}$ and $B \in \mathscr{G}$, the set $A \cap B \in d\mathcal{S}$. We will show that $d\mathcal{PS}^*$ is a syndetic, translation-invariant filter and appeal to \cref{lemma_condition_on_subfamily_of_ps_star} to see that $d\mathcal{PS}^* \subseteq \mathcal{PS}^*$, whereby $\mathcal{PS} \subseteq d\mathcal{PS}$. Translation invariance of $d\mathcal{PS}^*$ follows from the positive translation invariance of $d\mathcal{PS}$ shown in \cref{lemma_translates_of_dps_sets} \eqref{item_all_translates_are_dps}. That $d\mathcal{PS}^*$ is a filter is shown in \cref{lemma_dcps_dps_are_pr}. That every member of $d\mathcal{PS}^*$ is syndetic follows from the fact that $\mathcal{T} \subseteq d\mathcal{T} \subseteq d\mathcal{PS}$, whereby the family $d\mathcal{PS}^*$ is syndetic.

nodes.statement: Let $A \in d\mathcal{PS}$. By \cref{thm_dcps_and_dps_are_ps}, the set $A$ is piecewise syndetic. By \cref{lem:central_characterization}, there exists a minimal system $(X,T)$, a point $x \in X$, a nonempty, open set $U \subseteq X$, and a thick set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A \supseteq R(x,U) \cap H$. For all $n \in R(x,U)$, we see that the set $A - n \supseteq R(T^n x, U) \cap (H-n)$, which, by \cref{lem:central_characterization}, is central. Thus, the set in \eqref{eqn_translates_of_dps_set_to_central} contains $R(x,U) \in d\mathcal{S}$, as was to be shown. To arrive at the same result when $A-n$ is replaced by $A+n$, begin by writing $A \supseteq R(x,U) \cap H$ in the same way, noting that by \cref{lemma_may_assume_invertible}, we may assume that the system $(X,T)$ is invertible. We claim that the set $R_{T^{-1}}(x,U)$ is contained in the set in \eqref{eqn_translates_of_dps_set_to_central} with $A-n$ replaced by $A+n$. Since the system $(X,T^{-1})$ is minimal (see, for example, \cite[Lemma 2.7]{glasscock_koutsogiannis_richter_2019}), this will demonstrate that the set in \eqref{eqn_translates_of_dps_set_to_central} is dynamically syndetic. Suppose $n \in R_{T^{-1}}(x,U)$ so that $T^{-n} x \in U$. It is quick to check that $R(T^{-n}x,U) \cap \{n+1, n+2, \ldots\} \subseteq R(x,U) + n$. Since $R(T^{-n}x,U) \in dc\mathcal{S}$, it follows by \cref{lemma_ds_dcs_modifyable_on_a_finite_set} that the set $R(T^{-n}x,U) \cap \{n+1, n+2, \ldots\} \in dc\mathcal{S}$. It follows by \cref{lem:central_characterization} that the set \[A + n \supseteq \big(R(x,U) + n\big) \cap \big(H + n\big) \supseteq \big(R(T^{-n}x,U) \cap \{n+1, n+2, \ldots\}\big) \cap \big(H + n\big),\] is central, as desired. Finally, that \eqref{eqn_relationship_between_dps_and_c_classes} holds follows immediately from \eqref{eqn_translates_of_dps_set_to_central} for $A-n$ and $A+n$.

nodes.name: PS* is the largest family preserving dS, dT, PS under intersection
nodes.statement: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. The following conditions are equivalent to the set $A$ being thickly syndetic ($A \in \mathcal{PS}^*$): \begin{enumerate} \item for all $B \in d\mathcal{S}$, the set $A \cap B \in d\mathcal{S}$; \item for all $B \in d\mathcal{T}$, the set $A \cap B \in d\mathcal{T}$; \item for all $B \in \mathcal{PS}$, the set $A \cap B \in \mathcal{PS}$; \item for all $B \in \mathcal{PS}^*$, the set $A \cap B \in \mathcal{PS}^*$. \end{enumerate} Thus, the family $\mathcal{PS}^*$ is the largest family of sets that satisfies any one condition (equivalently, all conditions). Moreover, if the set $A$ is thickly syndetic, then \begin{enumerate} \setcounter{enumi}{4} \item for all $B \in dc\mathcal{S}$, the set $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{S}$; \item for all $B \in dc\mathcal{T}$, the set $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{T}$; \item for all $B \in dc\mathcal{PS}$, the set $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{PS}$; \item for all $B \in dc\mathcal{PS}^*$, the set $A \cap B \in dc\mathcal{PS}^*$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Family of polynomial multiple return-time sets
nodes.statement: Denote by $\mathscr{G}$ the upward closure of the family of all subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ of the form \begin{align} R \big(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E \big)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k \\ j = 1, \ldots, \ell}} \vcentcolon= \left\{ n \in \mathbb{N} \ \middle | \ \mu\left( \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n)} \right)^{-1} E \right) > 0 \right\}, \end{align} where $k, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$, the tuple $(X, \mu, T_1, \ldots, T_k)$ is an invertible, commuting probability measure preserving system, the set $E \subseteq X$ satisfies $\mu(E) > 0$, and, for $1 \leqslant i \leqslant k$, $1 \leqslant j \leqslant \ell$, the polynomial $p_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$ satisfies $p_{i,j}(\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $p_{i,j}(0) = 0$.

nodes.statement:
By a corollary of the IP Polynomial Szemer'{e}di{} Theorem of Bergelson and McCutcheon \cite[Thm. 7.12]{Bergelson-McCutcheon-IPpolynomialSzemeredi}, every member of $\mathscr{G}$ is an $\mathcal{IP}^*$ set. Therefore, the family $\mathscr{G}$ is $\mathcal{IP}^*$. To show that $\mathscr{G}$ is a filter, we must show that the set  egin{align} R  ig(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k \ j = 1, \ldots, \ell}} \cap R  ig(
u, S_i, q_{i,j}, F  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, r \ j = 1, \ldots, t}} \end{align} belongs to $\mathscr{G}$, where $(X, \mu, T_1, \ldots, T_k)$, $p_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$, $E \subseteq X$, $(Y, 
u, S_1, \ldots, S_r)$, $q_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$, and $F \subseteq Y$ are as described above. Denote by $I$ the identity transformation on both $X$ and $Y$, and consider the commuting probability measure preserving system \[ ig(X 	imes Y, \mu \otimes 
u, T_1 \otimes I, \ldots, T_k \otimes I, I \otimes S_1, \ldots, I \otimes S_r  ig).\] The set $E 	imes F \subseteq X 	imes Y$ satisfies $(\mu \otimes 
u)(E 	imes F) = \mu(E) 
u(F) > 0$. Moreover,  egin{gather*}  ig(\mu \otimes 
u  ig) \left(  igcap_{j_1=1}^{\ell}  igcap_{j_2=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} (T_i \otimes I)^{p_{i,j_1}(n)} \ \cdot \ \prod_{i=1}^{r} (I \otimes S_i)^{q_{i,j_2}(n)}ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) ight) = \  ig( \mu \otimes 
u  ig) \left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} (T_i \otimes I)^{p_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) \ \cap \  igcap_{j=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{r} (I \otimes S_i)^{q_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) ight) = \ \mu\left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} E ight) \ \cdot \ 
u\left(  igcap_{j=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{r} S_i^{q_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} F ight). \end{gather*} It follows that the set in \eqref{eqn_set_to_show_is_filter} is equal to \[R  ig( \mu \otimes 
u, U_i, m_{i,j}, E 	imes F  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k+r \ j = 1, \ldots, \ell t}},\] where \[U_i \vcentcolon=  egin{cases} T_i \otimes I & 	ext{ if $i \leqslant k$} \ I \otimes S_{i-k} & 	ext{ if $i > k$}\end{cases}, \qquad 	ext{ and } \qquad m_{i,j} \vcentcolon=  egin{cases} p_{i, (j 	ext{ mod } \ell) + 1} & 	ext{ if $i \leqslant k$} \ q_{i-k, \lceil j / \ell ceil} & 	ext{ if $i > k$}\end{cases}.\] This shows that the set in \eqref{eqn_set_to_show_is_filter} belongs to $\mathscr{G}$, as desired. Next, we will show that $\mathscr{G}$ is idempotent. It suffices by \cref{rmk_showing_idempotency} to show that if $D$ is a set of the form in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set}, then $D \subseteq D - \mathscr{G}$, that is, for all $m \in D$, the set $D-m \in \mathscr{G}$. Let $D$ be a set of the form in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set}, and let $m \in D$. Define \[ E' \vcentcolon=  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(m)} ight)^{-1} E. \] Since $m \in D$, we have that $\mu(E') > 0$. For $i = 1, \ldots, k$ and $j = 1, \ldots, \ell$, define $q_{i,j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$ by \[ q_{i,j}(n) \vcentcolon= p_{i,j}(n + m) - p_{i,j}(m). \] Note that $q_{i,j}(\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $q_{i,j}(0) = 0$. By expanding the definition of $E'$, we get  egin{align*}  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{q_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} E' &=  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m) - p_{i,j}(m)} ight)^{-1} E' \ &=  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m) - p_{i,j}(m)} ight)^{-1} \left(  igcap_{j'=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i'=1}^{k} T_{i'}^{p_{i',j'}(m)} ight)^{-1} E ight) \ &\subseteq  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m)} ight)^{-1} E. \end{align*} It follows that \[ R  ig(\mu, T_i, q_{i,j}, E'  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k \ j = 1, \ldots, \ell}} \subseteq \left\{n \in \mathbb{N} \ \middle | \ \mu \left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m)} ight)^{-1} E ight) > 0 ight\} = D - m, \] whereby $D-m \in \mathscr{G}$, as desired.

nodes.name: Filter: intersection of two return sets is a return set of the product
nodes.statement:
To show that $\mathscr{G}$ is a filter, we must show that the set  egin{align} R  ig(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k \ j = 1, \ldots, \ell}} \cap R  ig(
u, S_i, q_{i,j}, F  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, r \ j = 1, \ldots, t}} \end{align} belongs to $\mathscr{G}$, where $(X, \mu, T_1, \ldots, T_k)$, $p_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$, $E \subseteq X$, $(Y, 
u, S_1, \ldots, S_r)$, $q_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$, and $F \subseteq Y$ are as described above. Denote by $I$ the identity transformation on both $X$ and $Y$, and consider the commuting probability measure preserving system \[ ig(X 	imes Y, \mu \otimes 
u, T_1 \otimes I, \ldots, T_k \otimes I, I \otimes S_1, \ldots, I \otimes S_r  ig).\] The set $E 	imes F \subseteq X 	imes Y$ satisfies $(\mu \otimes 
u)(E 	imes F) = \mu(E) 
u(F) > 0$. Moreover,  egin{gather*}  ig(\mu \otimes 
u  ig) \left(  igcap_{j_1=1}^{\ell}  igcap_{j_2=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} (T_i \otimes I)^{p_{i,j_1}(n)} \ \cdot \ \prod_{i=1}^{r} (I \otimes S_i)^{q_{i,j_2}(n)}ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) ight) = \  ig( \mu \otimes 
u  ig) \left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} (T_i \otimes I)^{p_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) \ \cap \  igcap_{j=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{r} (I \otimes S_i)^{q_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} (E 	imes F) ight) = \ \mu\left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} E ight) \ \cdot \ 
u\left(  igcap_{j=1}^{t} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{r} S_i^{q_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} F ight). \end{gather*} It follows that the set in \eqref{eqn_set_to_show_is_filter} is equal to \[R  ig( \mu \otimes 
u, U_i, m_{i,j}, E 	imes F  ig)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k+r \ j = 1, \ldots, \ell t}},\] where \[U_i \vcentcolon=  egin{cases} T_i \otimes I & 	ext{ if $i \leqslant k$} \ I \otimes S_{i-k} & 	ext{ if $i > k$}\end{cases}, \qquad 	ext{ and } \qquad m_{i,j} \vcentcolon=  egin{cases} p_{i, (j 	ext{ mod } \ell) + 1} & 	ext{ if $i \leqslant k$} \ q_{i-k, \lceil j / \ell ceil} & 	ext{ if $i > k$}\end{cases}.\] This shows that the set in \eqref{eqn_set_to_show_is_filter} belongs to $\mathscr{G}$, as desired.

nodes.name: Reduce idempotency to generators (Remark 2.5)
nodes.statement: Next, we will show that $\mathscr{G}$ is idempotent. It suffices by \cref{rmk_showing_idempotency} to show that if $D$ is a set of the form in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set}, then $D \subseteq D - \mathscr{G}$, that is, for all $m \in D$, the set $D-m \in \mathscr{G}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce idempotency to generators (Remark 2.5).

nodes.name: Define E' and shifted polynomials q_{i,j}
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a set of the form in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set}, and let $m \in D$. Define \[ E' \vcentcolon= \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(m)} \right)^{-1} E. \] Since $m \in D$, we have that $\mu(E') > 0$. For $i = 1, \ldots, k$ and $j = 1, \ldots, \ell$, define $q_{i,j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$ by \[ q_{i,j}(n) \vcentcolon= p_{i,j}(n + m) - p_{i,j}(m). \] Note that $q_{i,j}(\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $q_{i,j}(0) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define E' and shifted polynomials q_{i,j}.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Polynomial set recurrence: a proof of \texorpdfstring{H}{Theorem H}

nodes.name: The return set of E' under q lies in D - m
nodes.statement: By expanding the definition of $E'$, we get \begin{align*} \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{q_{i,j}(n)} \right)^{-1} E' &= \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m) - p_{i,j}(m)} \right)^{-1} E' \\ &= \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m) - p_{i,j}(m)} \right)^{-1} \left( \bigcap_{j'=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i'=1}^{k} T_{i'}^{p_{i',j'}(m)} \right)^{-1} E \right) \\ &\subseteq \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m)} \right)^{-1} E. \end{align*} It follows that \[ R \big(\mu, T_i, q_{i,j}, E' \big)_{\substack{i = 1, \ldots, k \\ j = 1, \ldots, \ell}} \subseteq \left\{n \in \mathbb{N} \ \middle | \ \mu \left( \bigcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{p_{i,j}(n+m)} \right)^{-1} E \right) > 0 \right\} = D - m, \] whereby $D-m \in \mathscr{G}$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: The return set of E' under q lies in D - m.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Polynomial set recurrence: a proof of \texorpdfstring{H}{Theorem H}

nodes.name: dcPS sets are sets of polynomial multiple recurrence (invertible case)
nodes.statement: Every $dc\mathcal{PS}$ set is a $\mathscr{G}^*$ set, that is, dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets are sets of polynomial multiple measurable recurrence for invertible commuting transformations.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Polynomial set recurrence: a proof of \texorpdfstring{H}{Theorem H}
conclusions: Every $dc\mathcal{PS}$ set is a $\mathscr{G}^*$ set, that is, dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets are sets of polynomial multiple measurable recurrence for invertible commuting transformations.
nodes.label: thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec

nodes.statement: By \cref{lemma_localization_is_syndetic_idempotent_filter}, the family $\mathscr{G}$ is a $\mathcal{C}^*$, idempotent filter. Therefore, by \cref{cor_central_class_equalities}, we have that $\mathscr{G} \subseteq dc\mathcal{PS}^*$. Taking the dual, we see $dc\mathcal{PS} \subseteq \mathscr{G}^*$, as desired.

nodes.statement:
Denote by $\mathscr{F}$ the upward closure of the family of all subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ of the form in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set}, where $k, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$, the tuple $(X, \mu, T_1, \ldots, T_k)$ is a commuting probability measure preserving system, the set $E \subseteq X$ satisfies $\mu(E) > 0$, and, for $1 \leqslant i \leqslant k$, $1 \leqslant j \leqslant \ell$, the polynomial $p_{i, j} \in \mathbb{Q}[n]$ satisfies $p_{i,j}(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq \mathbb{N}_0$ and $p_{i,j}(0) = 0$. To prove \cref{thm:dcps_multiple_recurrence}, we must show that $dc\mathcal{PS} \subseteq \mathscr{F}^*$. Let $A \in dc\mathcal{PS}$ and let $B \in \mathscr{F}$. The set $B$ contains a set of the form $R  ig(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E  ig)$ as described in the previous paragraph. By the measurable natural extension (cf. \cite[Lemma 7.11]{Bergelson-McCutcheon-IPpolynomialSzemeredi}), there exists an invertible, commuting probability measure preserving system $(Y, 
u, S_1, \ldots, S_k)$ and a measurable set $F \subseteq Y$ such that for all $n_{i, j} \in \mathbb{N}_0$, $1 \leqslant i \leqslant k$, $1 \leqslant j \leqslant \ell$,  egin{align} 
u \left(  igcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} S_i^{n_{i,j}} ight)^{-1} F ight) = \mu \left(  igcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{n_{i,j}} ight)^{-1} E ight). \end{align} By \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec}, there exists $n \in A$ such that \[
u\left(  igcap_{j=1}^{\ell} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} S_i^{p_{i,j}(n)} ight)^{-1} F ight) > 0.\] It follows from \eqref{eqn_measurable_natural_extension} that $n \in R  ig(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E  ig)$, showing that $A \cap B 
eq \emptyset$, as desired.

To prove \cref{thm:dcps_multiple_recurrence}, we must show that $dc\mathcal{PS} \subseteq \mathscr{F}^*$.

Let $A \in dc\mathcal{PS}$ and let $B \in \mathscr{F}$. The set $B$ contains a set of the form $R  ig(\mu, T_i, p_{i,j}, E  ig)$ as described in the previous paragraph. u, S_1, \ldots, S_k)$ and a measurable set $F \subseteq Y$ such that for all $n_{i, j} \in \mathbb{N}_0$, $1 \leqslant i \leqslant k$, $1 \leqslant j \leqslant \ell$,  egin{align} 
u \left(  igcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} S_i^{n_{i,j}} ight)^{-1} F ight) = \mu \left(  igcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{n_{i,j}} ight)^{-1} E ight). \end{align} By \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec}, there exists $n \in A$ such that \[

nodes.statement: \nu \left( \bigcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} S_i^{n_{i,j}} \right)^{-1} F \right) = \mu \left( \bigcap_{j=1}^\ell \left( \prod_{i=1}^{k} T_i^{n_{i,j}} \right)^{-1} E \right).

nodes.name: Comparison with the IP polynomial Szemerédi theorem
nodes.statement: The $\mathcal{IP}$ polynomial Szemer\'{e}di{} theorem \cite[Thm 7.12]{Bergelson-McCutcheon-IPpolynomialSzemeredi} shows that $\mathscr{G}$ is an $\mathcal{IP}^*$ family, while \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec} shows that $\mathscr{G}$ is an $dc\mathcal{PS}^*$ family. Because there is no containment in either direction between the families $\mathcal{IP}^*$ and $dc\mathcal{PS}^*$, \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec} is neither an upgrade nor an immediate corollary of the $\mathcal{IP}$ polynomial Szemer\'{e}di{} theorem. An upgrade to the conclusion of the $\mathcal{IP}$ polynomial Szemer\'{e}di{} theorem is available in the case that the polynomials in \eqref{eqn_poly_return_set} are required to be linear. In that case, the family $\mathscr{G}$ can be shown to be $\mathcal{IP}_0^*$ (see \cref{sec_open_quests_dps_sets} for a definition of the family $\mathcal{IP}_0^*$) by a corollary of a result of Furstenberg and Katznelson \cite[Thm. 10.3]{furstenberg_katznelson_1985}. The relationship between the families $dc\mathcal{PS}^*$ and $\mathcal{IP}_0^*$ is not known; it may be the case that $\mathcal{IP}_0^* \subseteq dc\mathcal{PS}^*$, for example. See \cref{ques:pointwise_recurrence_IP_0} below for more discussion in this direction.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Polynomial set recurrence: a proof of \texorpdfstring{H}{Theorem H}

nodes.name: dcPS sets contain polynomial Brauer configurations
nodes.statement: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be dynamically central piecewise syndetic. For all $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ with $p_i(\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $p_i(0) = 0$, there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ such that \begin{align} x, y, x + p_1(y), \ldots, x + p_k(y) \in A. \end{align}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 Dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets contain polynomial Brauer configurations
assumptions: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be dynamically central piecewise syndetic.
conclusions: there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ such that

nodes.name: Polynomial Brauer configuration
nodes.statement: x, y, x + p_1(y), \ldots, x + p_k(y) \in A.

nodes.statement: By \cref{thm_dcps_and_dps_are_ps}, the set $A$ is piecewise syndetic and hence has positive upper Banach density, $d^*(A) > 0$. By a standard application of the Furstenberg Correspondence Principle (\cite[Thm. 1.1]{Furstenberg-ErgodicBehavior}, see also \cite[Thm. 3.2.5]{mccutcheon_1999}), there exists an invertible probability measure preserving system $(X, \mu, T)$ and a set $E \subseteq X$ with $\mu(E) \geqslant d^*(A) > 0$ such that for all $n_1, \ldots, n_k \in \mathbb{Z}$, \begin{align*} \mu \big(T^{-n_1} E \cap \cdots \cap T^{-n_k} E \big) \leqslant d^* \big( (A-n_1) \cap \cdots \cap (A-n_k) \big). \end{align*} Setting $p_0 \equiv 0$, by \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec}, there exists $y \in A$ such that \[ 0 < \mu \big(E \cap T^{-p_1(y)} E \cap \cdots \cap T^{-p_k(y)} E \big) \leqslant d^* \big( A \cap (A-p_1(y)) \cap \cdots \cap (A-p_k(y)) \big). \] Therefore, there exist (many) $x \in A$ for which \eqref{eqn_poly_brauer_in_dcps} holds, as was to be shown.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 Dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets contain polynomial Brauer configurations
nodes.statement_short: A has positive upper Banach density (Theorem 5.11); the Furstenberg correspondence principle and Theorem 5.15 give y ∈ A with A ∩ ⋂(A - p_i(y)) of positive density.

nodes.name: Positive density and Furstenberg correspondence
nodes.statement: By \cref{thm_dcps_and_dps_are_ps}, the set $A$ is piecewise syndetic and hence has positive upper Banach density, $d^*(A) > 0$. By a standard application of the Furstenberg Correspondence Principle (\cite[Thm. 1.1]{Furstenberg-ErgodicBehavior}, see also \cite[Thm. 3.2.5]{mccutcheon_1999}), there exists an invertible probability measure preserving system $(X, \mu, T)$ and a set $E \subseteq X$ with $\mu(E) \geqslant d^*(A) > 0$ such that for all $n_1, \ldots, n_k \in \mathbb{Z}$, \begin{align*} \mu \big(T^{-n_1} E \cap \cdots \cap T^{-n_k} E \big) \leqslant d^* \big( (A-n_1) \cap \cdots \cap (A-n_k) \big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Positive density and Furstenberg correspondence.

nodes.name: Generalization to other group actions
nodes.statement: To which other group and semigroup actions do the main results in this paper generalize? For example, a generalization of \cref{thm_dcs_iff_cs} to $\mathbb{Z}$ might read: a subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ is dynamically central syndetic if and only if it is a member of a syndetic, idempotent filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 6 Open questions
nodes.label: quest_generalizations_to_other_grps

nodes.name: Odd 2-adic valuation set is dcS though x is not in U
nodes.statement: Recall example \eqref{item_dcs_two_adic_example} in \cref{sec_dy_synd_def_and_char}: the set $A$ of positive integers with even 2-adic valuation is dynamically central syndetic because the point $1_{A \cup \{0\}}$ is uniformly recurrent in the full shift $(\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}_0},\sigma)$ and $A = R_\sigma(1_{A \cup \{0\}}, [1]_0)$ where $1_{A \cup \{0\}} \in [1]_0$. Since $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ is the disjoint union of the cylinders $[0]_0$ and $[1]_0$, by properties of the 2-adic valuation, we see that \[A / 2 = \mathbb{N} \backslash A = R_\sigma(1_{A \cup \{0\}}, [0]_0).\] By \cref{lemma_dilates_of_dsyndetic_sets}, this set is dynamically central syndetic despite the fact that $1_{A \cup \{0\}} \not\in [0]_0$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Characterize when R(x,U) is dynamically central syndetic
nodes.statement: Let $(X,T)$ be a minimal system, $x \in X$, and $U \subseteq X$ be nonempty and open. Give necessary and sufficient conditions for $x$ and $U$ so that the set $R(x,U)$ is dynamically central syndetic.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
nodes.label: quest_nec_and_suff_for_rxu_dcs

nodes.name: Central return sets via proximality
nodes.statement: Indeed, if $U \subseteq X$ is clopen, then the set $R(x,U)$ is central if and only if $U$ contains a point proximal to $x$ (recall the definition of proximal from \cref{sec_ip_and_central_sets}).
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Proximality via idempotent ultrafilters
nodes.statement: It is a fact \cite[Lem. 19.22, Thms. 19.23, 19.25]{hindman_strauss_book_2012} that a pair of points $x, y \in X$ is proximal if and only if there exists an idempotent ultrafilter $p \in \beta \mathbb{N}$ such that $T^p x = y$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Proof of the proximality criterion for central return sets
nodes.statement: If $R(x,U)$ is central, then it belongs to a minimal, idempotent ultrafilter $p$, and so $T^p x \in \overline{U} = U$. On the other hand, if $x$ is proximal to a point $y \in U$, then there is a minimal, idempotent ultrafilter $p$ such that $T^p x = y$, and so $R(x,U) \in p$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
nodes.statement_short: Use the Hindman-Strauss characterization of proximality by idempotent ultrafilters in both directions.

nodes.name: IP* idempotent filters and distal points
nodes.statement: Does every member of an $\mathcal{IP}^*$, idempotent filter contain a set of the form $R(x,U)$, where $(X,T)$ is a minimal system, $x \in X$ is a distal point, and $U \subseteq X$ is an open neighborhood of $x$?
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
nodes.label: question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal

nodes.name: Furstenberg: characterization of distal points
nodes.statement: \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal} is motivated by a result of Furstenberg \cite[Thm 9.11]{furstenberg_book_1981}: a point $x \in X$ is a distal point if and only if for all open neighborhoods $U \subseteq X$ of $x$, the set $R(x,U)$ belongs to $\mathcal{IP}^*$ if and only if for all open neighborhoods $U \subseteq X$ of $x$, the set $R(x,U)$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}^*$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Conditional: sets of distal pointwise recurrence are translates of IP sets
nodes.statement: Suppose the answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal} is positive. If $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a set of pointwise recurrence for all distal points (ie., for all systems $(X,T)$, all distal $x \in X$, and all open $U \subseteq X$ containing $x$, the set $A \cap R(x,U) \neq \emptyset$), then there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $A - n \in \mathcal{IP}$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
assumptions: Suppose the answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal} is positive.
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a set of pointwise recurrence for all distal points
conclusions: there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $A - n \in \mathcal{IP}$.

nodes.statement: Consider the family \begin{align*} \mathscr{F} &\vcentcolon= \big\{ A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \ \big | \ \exists \ \ell \in \mathbb{N}, \ \ A-\ell \in \mathcal{IP} \big\}. \end{align*} Using the fact that the family $\mathcal{IP}$ is partition regular, it is not hard to show that \begin{align*} \mathscr{F}^* &= \big\{ B \subseteq \mathbb{N} \ \big | \ \forall \ \ell \in \mathbb{N}, \ B \cap (B-1) \cap \cdots \cap (B-\ell) \in \mathcal{IP}^* \big\}. \end{align*} The family $\mathscr{F}^*$ is an $\mathcal{IP}^*$, translation-invariant (hence, idempotent) filter. Suppose $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a set of pointwise recurrence for all distal points. We will use the positive answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal} to show that $A \in \mathscr{F}$ and conclude the proof of the lemma. To show that $A \in \mathscr{F}$, we will show that $A \in (\mathscr{F}^*)^*$. Let $B \in \mathscr{F}^*$. We must show that $A \cap B \neq \emptyset$. By the positive answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal}, the set $B$ contains the times of returns of a distal point to a neighborhood of itself. By assumption, the set $A \cap B \neq \emptyset$, as was to be shown.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
nodes.statement_short: The family of translates of IP sets has an IP*, translation-invariant dual filter; a positive answer to Question 6.3 puts each of its members' return sets of distal points inside, which A meets.

nodes.name: Define F (translates of IP sets) and describe F* as an IP*, translatio
nodes.statement: Consider the family \begin{align*} \mathscr{F} &\vcentcolon= \big\{ A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \ \big | \ \exists \ \ell \in \mathbb{N}, \ \ A-\ell \in \mathcal{IP} \big\}. \end{align*} Using the fact that the family $\mathcal{IP}$ is partition regular, it is not hard to show that \begin{align*} \mathscr{F}^* &= \big\{ B \subseteq \mathbb{N} \ \big | \ \forall \ \ell \in \mathbb{N}, \ B \cap (B-1) \cap \cdots \cap (B-\ell) \in \mathcal{IP}^* \big\}. \end{align*} The family $\mathscr{F}^*$ is an $\mathcal{IP}^*$, translation-invariant (hence, idempotent) filter.
nodes.statement_short: Define F (translates of IP sets) and describe F* as an IP*, translation-invariant filter.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Reduce to showing A ∈ F
nodes.statement: Suppose $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a set of pointwise recurrence for all distal points. We will use the positive answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal} to show that $A \in \mathscr{F}$ and conclude the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing A ∈ F.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Members of F* contain distal return sets, which A meets
nodes.statement: To show that $A \in \mathscr{F}$, we will show that $A \in (\mathscr{F}^*)^*$. Let $B \in \mathscr{F}^*$. We must show that $A \cap B \neq \emptyset$. By the positive answer to \cref{question_cstar_idempo_filter_implies_pt_distal}, the set $B$ contains the times of returns of a distal point to a neighborhood of itself. By assumption, the set $A \cap B \neq \emptyset$, as was to be shown.
nodes.statement_short: Members of F* contain distal return sets, which A meets.
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets

nodes.name: Is dcS + dcS = dcS?
nodes.statement: Is it the case that \[dc\mathcal{S} = dc\mathcal{S} + dc\mathcal{S}?\] Because it is known that $dc\mathcal{S} \subseteq dc\mathcal{S} + dc\mathcal{S}$, it is equivalent to ask: If $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is such that the set \[A - dc\mathcal{S} \vcentcolon= \big\{ n \in \mathbb{N} \ \big | \ A - n \in dc\mathcal{S} \big\}\] is dynamically central syndetic, is $A$ dynamically central syndetic?
nodes.section: 6.1 Dynamically syndetic sets
nodes.label: quest_is_dcs_plus_dcs_equal_to_dcs

nodes.name: Alternative characterization of pointwise recurrence
nodes.statement: Is it true that a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a set of pointwise recurrence if and only if for all $B \in dc\mathcal{S}$, there exists $n \in A$ such that $B-n \in dc\mathcal{S}$?
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
nodes.label: quest_alt_char_of_dcthick

nodes.name: Relatives of the alternative characterization question
nodes.statement: There are several other relatives of \cref{quest_alt_char_of_dcthick} that are of interest. \begin{enumerate} \item Is it true that a set $A \in d\mathcal{T}$ if and only if for all $B \in d\mathcal{S}$, there exists $n \in A$ such that $B-n \in dc\mathcal{S}$? Equivalently: is it true that $A \in d\mathcal{S}$ if and only if there exists $B \in d\mathcal{S}$ such that $B - dc\mathcal{S} \subseteq A$? \item Is it true that a set $A \in dc\mathcal{T}$ if and only if for all $B \in \mathcal{C}$, there exists $n \in A$ such that $B-n \in \mathcal{C}$? Equivalently: is it true that $A \in dc\mathcal{S}$ if and only if there exists $B \in \mathcal{C}$ such that $B - \mathcal{C} \subseteq A$? \item Is it true that a set $A \in d\mathcal{T}$ if and only if for all $B \in \mathcal{PS}$, there exists $n \in A$ such that $B-n \in \mathcal{C}$? Equivalently: is it true that $A \in d\mathcal{S}$ if and only if there exists $B \in \mathcal{PS}$ such that $B - \mathcal{C} \subseteq A$?\\ \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets

nodes.name: Partitioning dynamically thick sets into two
nodes.statement: Can every dynamically thick set (resp. set of pointwise recurrence) be partitioned into two disjoint dynamically thick sets (resp. sets of pointwise recurrence)?
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
nodes.label: ques:partition_into_two_pointwise_recurrence

nodes.name: Countable robustly syndetic structure for dynamically thick sets
nodes.statement: Is it true that for all dynamically thick sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, there exists a countable, robustly syndetic collection $\mathscr{F}$ of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and, for all $B \in \mathscr{F}$, a thick set $H_B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, such that \begin{align} A = \bigcup_{B \in \mathscr{F}} \big( B \cap H_B \big)? \end{align}
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
nodes.label: quest_robust_synd_family

nodes.name: Enhanced form of a dynamically thick set
nodes.statement: A = \bigcup_{B \in \mathscr{F}} \big( B \cap H_B \big)?
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
nodes.label: eqn_enhanced_dt_form

nodes.name: Conditional: dynamically thick sets partition into two
nodes.statement: If the answer to \cref{quest_robust_synd_family} is positive, then every dynamically thick set can be partitioned into two disjoint dynamically thick sets.
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
conclusions: every dynamically thick set can be partitioned into two disjoint dynamically thick sets
nodes.label: lemma_solution_to_partition_problem

nodes.statement: Suppose the answer to \cref{quest_robust_synd_family} is positive. Let $A \in d\mathcal{T}$, and write the set $A$ in the form given in \eqref{eqn_enhanced_dt_form}. Enumerate $\mathscr{F}$ as $\{B_1, B_2, \ldots\}$. For ease of notation, for each $i \in \mathbb{N}$, write $H_i$ instead of $H_{B_i}$. By passing to subsets of the $H_i$'s, we may assume without loss of generality that $H_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, j}$ where $I_{i,j}$ are finite intervals in $\mathbb{N}$ satisfying $\lim_{j \to \infty} |I_{i,j}| = \infty$ and, for all $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, $\max I_{i,j} < \min I_{i, j+1}$. It is a simple exercise to choose positive integers \[n^{(1)}_1 < n^{(1)}_2 < n^{(2)}_1 < n^{(1)}_3 < n^{(2)}_2 < n^{(3)}_1 < n^{(1)}_4 < n^{(2)}_3 < n^{(3)}_2 < n^{(4)}_1 < \cdots\] so that the intervals $I_{i, n^{(i)}_j}$, $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, are disjoint. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, define two thick sets \[ H^{(1)}_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, n^{(i)}_{2j-1}} \quad \text{ and } \quad H^{(2)}_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, n^{(i)}_{2j}}. \] Let \[ A_1 = \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} \big(B_i \cap H^{(1)}_i \big) \quad \text{ and } \quad A_2 = \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} \big(B_i \cap H^{(2)}_i \big). \] By construction, the sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ are disjoint subsets of $A$. By appending $A \backslash (A_1 \cup A_2)$ to $A_1$, we get that $A = A_1 \cup A_2$. Moreover, both $A_1$ and $A_2$ have the form in \cref{cor_weak_structure_result}, and so they are dynamically thick.
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets
nodes.statement_short: Write A in the countable form, split each H_i into two thick sets by interleaving disjoint intervals, and use Theorem F.

nodes.name: Write A in the countable form with interval-structured H_i
nodes.statement: Suppose the answer to \cref{quest_robust_synd_family} is positive. Let $A \in d\mathcal{T}$, and write the set $A$ in the form given in \eqref{eqn_enhanced_dt_form}. Enumerate $\mathscr{F}$ as $\{B_1, B_2, \ldots\}$. For ease of notation, for each $i \in \mathbb{N}$, write $H_i$ instead of $H_{B_i}$. By passing to subsets of the $H_i$'s, we may assume without loss of generality that $H_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, j}$ where $I_{i,j}$ are finite intervals in $\mathbb{N}$ satisfying $\lim_{j \to \infty} |I_{i,j}| = \infty$ and, for all $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, $\max I_{i,j} < \min I_{i, j+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write A in the countable form with interval-structured H_i.
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets

nodes.name: Interleave intervals to split each H_i into two thick sets
nodes.statement: It is a simple exercise to choose positive integers \[n^{(1)}_1 < n^{(1)}_2 < n^{(2)}_1 < n^{(1)}_3 < n^{(2)}_2 < n^{(3)}_1 < n^{(1)}_4 < n^{(2)}_3 < n^{(3)}_2 < n^{(4)}_1 < \cdots\] so that the intervals $I_{i, n^{(i)}_j}$, $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$, are disjoint. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, define two thick sets \[ H^{(1)}_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, n^{(i)}_{2j-1}} \quad \text{ and } \quad H^{(2)}_i = \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} I_{i, n^{(i)}_{2j}}. \] Let \[ A_1 = \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} \big(B_i \cap H^{(1)}_i \big) \quad \text{ and } \quad A_2 = \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} \big(B_i \cap H^{(2)}_i \big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Interleave intervals to split each H_i into two thick sets.
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets

nodes.name: The two resulting sets partition A and are dynamically thick by Theore
nodes.statement: By construction, the sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ are disjoint subsets of $A$. By appending $A \backslash (A_1 \cup A_2)$ to $A_1$, we get that $A = A_1 \cup A_2$. Moreover, both $A_1$ and $A_2$ have the form in \cref{cor_weak_structure_result}, and so they are dynamically thick.
nodes.statement_short: The two resulting sets partition A and are dynamically thick by Theorem F.
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets

nodes.name: σ-compact weakening of the robust syndetic structure question
nodes.statement: Such a modification to \cref{quest_robust_synd_family} could be: \emph{Is there is a collection $\mathscr{F}$ with the property that $\{ 1_B \ | \ B \in \mathscr{F}\}$ is a $\sigma$-compact subset of $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ and, for all $B \in \mathscr{F}$, a thick set $H_B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that the map $\mathscr{F} \to \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ given by $B \mapsto H_B$ is continuous such that $A$ has the form in \eqref{eqn_enhanced_dt_form}?}
nodes.section: 6.2 Dynamically thick sets

nodes.name: Are dcPS sets IP_0 sets?
nodes.statement: Must every dynamically central piecewise syndetic set be an $\mathcal{IP}_0$ set?
nodes.section: 6.3 Dynamically piecewise syndetic sets
nodes.label: ques:pointwise_recurrence_IP_0

nodes.name: Do dynamically thick sets contain IP_3 configurations?
nodes.statement: A simpler variant of \cref{ques:pointwise_recurrence_IP_0} is: \emph{Must dynamically thick sets contain configurations of the form $\{x,y,z, x+y,x+z,y+z, x+y+z\}$?}
nodes.section: 6.3 Dynamically piecewise syndetic sets

nodes.name: Upgrade Bergelson-McCutcheon from IP* to IP_0*
nodes.statement: To recover the full result in \cref{thm_dcps_is_poly_mult_comm_rec} via this line of reasoning would require an answer to a long-standing open question: \emph{Can the results of Bergelson and McCutcheon (eg. \cite[Thm. 7.12]{Bergelson-McCutcheon-IPpolynomialSzemeredi}) be upgraded from $\mathcal{IP}^*$ to $\mathcal{IP}_0^*$?}
nodes.section: 6.3 Dynamically piecewise syndetic sets

nodes.name: Is dcPS idempotent?
nodes.statement: Is the family of dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets idempotent, that is, \[dc\mathcal{PS} \subseteq dc\mathcal{PS} + dc\mathcal{PS}?\]
nodes.section: 6.3 Dynamically piecewise syndetic sets
nodes.label: quest_is_dcps_idempotent
